messages:
anya: Noticed a tiny but nasty mismatch in the API ref for /v1/generate when returning structured JSON responses. The docs example shows responses with Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8, but our runtime now emits application/json without charset. Some Java HTTP clients choke on the charset assumption in the samples.

anya: Current docs snippet (response example header):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
```

anya: Actual service header we see in traces:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
```

mike: Oof. We added a proxy layer that strips the charset header to reduce header size. Docs should avoid implying the charset. Also the Java snippet in quickstart uses new String(respBody, "UTF-8") which paired with the docs header made users think they must manually decode. We should show using InputStreamReader / charset detection or recommend the SDK helper.

kevin: Agreed. Small PR looks best: update response header examples to omit charset, update Java snippet to use resp.getEntity().getContent() + InputStreamReader with StandardCharsets.UTF_8, and add a note: "Clients: server returns application/json; handle encoding per your HTTP client (most clients default to UTF-8). Use official SDKs to avoid low-level parsing."

anya: I opened PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/12802. Also added a one-line compatibility note in migration guide: "Do not rely on docs showing charset in Content-Type; server may omit charset."

mike: Can you paste the updated Java snippet here? I'll sanity-check.

anya: New Java example:
```java
// recommended raw HTTP (defensive)
HttpResponse resp = client.execute(req);
InputStream in = resp.getEntity().getContent();
try (BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(in, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))) {
  StringBuilder sb = new StringBuilder();
  String line;
  while ((line = br.readLine()) != null) {
    sb.append(line);
  }
  JSONObject json = new JSONObject(sb.toString());
  System.out.println(json.get("choices"));
}
```
kevin: That looks good. Also add a short Node/Python one-liner using SDK to drive home the recommendation.

anya: Added SDK examples and left an explicit raw-HTTP example for teams that need it. Also updated the response example block to:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json
```

doc-bot: docs lint OK for branch fix/response-charset. (files changed: api/generate.md, quickstart/java.md, migration/compat.md)

mike: Can we add a docs test that ensures response headers in examples do not contain "charset=" to avoid reverting?

kevin: Yes I'll add a grep test in docs/spec: assert not("charset=" in example_headers). That should be lightweight.

staging-bot: Deployed fix/response-charset to staging at 1916781300 (sha: ffeedd0). Preview: https://docs-staging.redwood.ai/api/generate#responses

anya: Preview looks good; Java snippet renders and the Content-Type examples match runtime. Assigning follow-ups: kevin -> add docs test, mike -> notify Support about customers who copied raw header parsing. Closing once tests merge. :white_check_mark:
